commitments.text:
1.  NCL shall cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed and operated in accordance with 
the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate, collectively comprising NCL’s application 
of July 24, 1996.

3.  NCL must fulfil all commitments and proposed mitigation measures as documented in their 
application dated July 24, 1996, including commitments and measures contained in 
supplementary documents and correspondence listed in Schedule A to this Certificate.

4.  Despite Condition 1 above, if prior to the processing of the first 1,130 thousand cubic metres of 
sour natural gas, NCL requires variation in the Project design, location, construction or operation 
outlined in the documents in Schedule A to this Certificate:
a). NCL shall make application for such variation to authorities required to give approvals, licenses, 
permits or other authorizations under other enactments for implementation of the Project, in accordance 
with that authority’s approval process, unless:
i) the variation would be subject to provisions of the Environmental Assessment Reviewable Projects 
Regulation (B.C. Reg. 276/95) if the Project was constructed and operational; or
ii) the variation is a modification:
a) to the acid gas disposal scheme as documented in Schedule A to this Certificate;
b) to the location of the natural gas processing plant outside the boundary of the site as 
proposed by NCL and documented in Schedule A to this Certificate;
c) to the location of the raw gas gathering line along a route other than as documented in 
correspondence dated October 31, 1996 listed in Schedule A to this Certificate;
d) to the number of pipelines, their diameter or function; or
e) requiring the installation of facilities on or off the main site of the Project which were 
not identified in the application, dated July 24, 1996, and documented in Schedule A to 
this Certificate.
b) For the changes listed in condition 4a) i and ii, NCL shall:
i) provide notice of the proposed change to the Executive Director; and
ii) where the Executive Director, in consultation with the appropriate provincial 
authorities, considers that the change may have the potential for significant adverse effects, 
provide the Executive Director with plans, analyses, records and other information 
necessary for an effective assessment by the Executive Director of the proposed change.
c) Where the Executive Director, following receipt of and evaluation of information requested from NCL 
under Condition 4 (b), considers that the proposed change could cause significant adverse effects, the 
Executive Director may:
i) make a recommendation to the Minister and the Responsible Minister as to a review 
process necessary for an effective assessment of the potential effects of the change, and 
where the effects are potentially adverse, whether those effects may be mitigated;

5. NCL must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, have substantially started and constructed the 
Project within five years of the issue date of this Certificate.
